subject: Human Body
title: Alzheimer's Disease
description: A micro-lesson that makes Alzheimer's Disease usable.

hook.text: Alzheimer's steals memories one at a time.

buildup.text: Amyloid plaques and tau tangles build up in the brain. Neurons die and brain tissue visibly shrinks over time.

discovery.text: The hippocampus is hit first. That's why new memories vanish before old ones. The disease works backward through time.

twist.text: Symptoms appear 20 years after plaques start forming. By the time memory fails, massive damage has already occurred.

climax.text: No cure exists yet. New drugs aim to clear plaques early, but the disease remains one of medicine's greatest challenges.

punchline.text: Memories disappear in reverse. Recent goes first. Childhood lasts.

quiz.question: Why do new memories vanish before old ones in Alzheimer's?
options: Old memories are stored in stronger neurons
The hippocampus, which forms new memories, is hit first
